Uncle,
Twelve years have passed since that night in the Buddhist hall when you and I had our secret talk.

Back then, you said, "Lu Bo, since you've taken up this banner, I entrust you with three tasks."
I agreed without hesitation, thinking that nothing in this world is impossible if I put my heart into it.

The first task was to ensure the Commoners' warmth and sustenance; the second, to safeguard peace at the border.
We made a pact: if the harvest was bountiful, I would cast a ceremonial vessel depicting six prosperous livestock and send it to Chang'an. But you said four would suffice, and that the auspicious metal should instead be used to forge farming tools for the Commoners.
As for the third task... you told me to wait until I accomplished the first two before revealing it.

Now, the newly sprouted crops in the borderlands show the first signs of green, and Liangzhou has been restored. The two tasks entrusted to me are complete, but what, exactly, was the third task you never spoke of?

Access to the market tower requires official rank. From below, one can control the market with the drum; from above, one can oversee it all. Thus, the tower stands tallest, offering a full view from its peak.
